Day and Residential Special Needs School for pupils with Vision and Sensory Impairment
Co-Head Teachers' Welcome
On behalf of Linden Lodge, we are delighted to welcome you to our website. Our staff, governors, children and families work together to create the positive atmosphere and high standards that characterise our school community. We are a dynamic and successful school where diversity and individuality are celebrated.
Our values underpin everything we do at Linden Lodge. We have created an ambitious culture through which we achieve the highest standards by promoting partnership working and building a positive and supportive environment where individuals flourish. Above all we see each student as an individual and celebrate all achievements as a community.
We offer a highly specialised curriculum that enables children and young people with vision and sensory impairment to engage, achieve and be prepared for life as active citizens. Our curriculum is underpinned by an inter-disciplinary approach where professionals, therapists, habilitation officers, nursing, support staff and specialist teachers work collaboratively to build a personalised provision for all students.
Therapy at Linden Lodge strives to support you, the pupil, in achieving your potential. The unique support we provide, from the moment you enter the school through to preparation for adulthood, is steered by your aspirations, strengths and needs. We do this through specialist, individualised, hands-on therapy and advice led by a team of Speech and Language, Occupational, and Physiotherapists.
The residential provision at Linden Lodge School, offers both full time and part time boarding. The young people have access to the full facilities of the school’s provision. We operate a waking day curriculum to develop the young people’s interests and learning goals. The provision is supported by experienced staff; all young people have a key worker to enable them to develop their independence skills.

About Us
Linden Lodge School is a day and residential special needs school for students aged 2-19 with Vision and Multi Sensory Impairment. We are located in Southfields, and consider prospective students from a wide area.
We consider children and young people from nursery to year 14 with Vision Impairment, Hearing Impairment and Multi-Sensory Impairment. We also consider applications for pupils who would benefit from our sensory education approaches and facilities.
The education of pupils with Sensory Impairment is highly specialist and therefore we have specialist teachers, a specialist sensory curriculum and extensive specialist resources and facilities on our campus.
Our expectations for each pupil are high and we understand that each pupil with a Sensory Impairment has a unique diagnosis and learning profile. We have specialist centres for pupils with profound multiple learning needs and also for pupils following the National Curriculum and a range of GCSE, BTEC and externally accredited pathways.
We, therefore, offer a range of Curriculum pathways each tailored to pupils’ needs and abilities delivered through our departmental and specialist centres. A number of our centres are in separate purpose-built accommodation on site.
We want our pupils to reach their potential and achieve as much independence as possible. Every pupil has, in addition to their curriculum targets, personal goals to optimise their use of Vision, Hearing and other Senses.
If you feel that Linden Lodge School has the expertise and facilities that you are looking for please contact the Co-Headteachers to arrange a visit.

Careers Programme Information
Linden Lodge offers a comprehensive and personalised careers provision for students from Year 7 onwards, with a focus on helping young people with vision loss prepare for adulthood, further education, and employment. Here’s an overview of the key aspects of their Careers Provision:
1. Personalised Careers Guidance
2. Work Experience and Skill Development
3. Support for Individual Aspirations
4. Collaboration with External Partners
Linden Lodge’s approach aims to provide students with vision loss the necessary skills, experiences, and confidence to succeed in the workplace and live as independently as possible. Through personalised guidance, skill-building, and partnerships with specialised organisations, Linden Lodge helps prepare its students for a fulfilling and successful future.
Linden Lodge School partners with several external organisations and agencies to enhance its careers provision and support students with vision loss in their preparation for adulthood, further education, and employment. These partnerships enable the school to offer specialised resources and opportunities tailored to each student's needs. Here’s an overview of their key partnerships:
1. Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and Access to Work
2. Blind in Business
3. Additional Partner Organisations
Through these collaborations, Linden Lodge ensures that students benefit from a comprehensive support network, enhancing their readiness for employment and independent living.
Careers Opportunities
Whole School Provision from Y8 onwards
Students will be vocationally profiled by Careers Teacher. This marks the start of the Careers Journey.
Students will be actively encouraged and supported by teachers to investigate work places of interest.
Personalised Vocational Profile and Careers Portfolio
Annual Careers and Transition Fairs organised for different pathways
Enrichment Speakers visit school
Visits to work places
Work Experience within school internally: Linden Lodge Café Project.

Voluntary/ Charity Projects Locally:
Participate in Disability Awareness Training for Parents and Employers – Mencap Here I am.
Students to contribute to the Linden Lodge Case For Business which details statistics explaining the benefits of employing someone with a disability.
*Students will be actively encouraged and supported by teachers to investigate work places of interest during weekly Careers sessions with class teachers.
Students will begin internal work experience in Summer Term. This will give students a chance to begin to apply work skills learnt in class.
Students will continue internal work experience. Students will use personalised careers portfolio assessment to address any skills that need to be worked on and improved.
Students will now move onto external voluntary / work experience placements. Work experience projects should be long term so skills can be worked on and ideally weekly.
Students will now move onto external voluntary / work experience placements.
